global_caption: The video consists of 12 shots and presents a warm-toned, realistic woodworking tutorial. The overall aesthetic is dominated by warm wood tones and soft indoor lighting, complemented by natural side light from the workshop. Camera movement is steady and clear, emphasizing accurate presentation of tutorial steps. The
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a wide eye-level shot to present a clean woodworking workshop in full view. In the foreground, a workbench holds a tape measure, square, pencil, and clamps; the midground features wooden boards awaiting processing, while the background reveals a table saw and storage wall. Moderate depth of field clearly separates the layers of tools. Warm yellow lighting blends with natural light from the window, creating a stable, realistic wooden atmosphere. A middle-aged male carpenter stands beside the workbench, raising his hand to indicate today's project, while Chinese The camera slowly pushes in to establish a sense of being on-site for instruction.
shot2: The second shot is a hard cut from the previous one, using a close-up at eye level, with composition focused on several pine boards on the workbench. Blurred tools in the foreground form leading lines, while the midground clearly captures hands selecting wood based on grain and thickness. Warm lighting remains consistent as a middle-aged male carpenter picks up two pine boards to compare their edges and flatness, pointing at the board edges with his fingers and measuring length and width with a tape measure. The Chinese The camera performs a slight lateral follow, emphasizing the material selection logic.
shot3: Shot 3 cuts hard to a close-up overhead shot. The center of the frame is a flat wooden board, with ruler and pencil forming clear horizontal and vertical guides. Shallow depth of field sharpens scale markings and pencil tip. Under warm indoor lighting, wood grain details are visible. Chinese The scratch The camera maintains stable overhead framing with slight downward pressure to reinforce procedural rigor.
shot4: Shot 4 cuts hard to a close-up eye-level slightly low-angle shot, focusing on the clamp, board edge, and contact point with the workbench. Foreground shows the clamp knob, midground the board, background softly blurred. Warm lighting remains consistent. The carpenter tightens the clamp to secure the board firmly. The board slightly depresses under pressure before stabilizing. The camera performs a very short push-in to emphasize completion of the securing action.
shot5: Shot 5 cuts hard to a medium close-up eye-level shot. Foreground shows the edge of the safety guard, midground the hands feeding the board, background the wood shavings collection zone. Under warm lighting, metal and wood textures are distinct. Chinese The high-speed saw The camera smoothly tracks horizontally with the board’s motion, clearly showing the cutting path.
shot6: Shot 6 cuts hard to a close-up eye-level shot. The newly cut edge of the board dominates the frame. Foreground shows the plane blade edge, midground the hand’s pressure point, background softly blurred into warm workshop tones. Consistent side lighting casts soft highlights across the edge. The carpenter slowly pushes the plane to smooth the edge, thin shavings curling and falling onto the bench. The edge transitions from slightly rough to smooth. Chinese The planing The camera slightly follows the hand’s forward motion.
shot7: Shot 7 cuts hard to a close-up overhead slightly angled shot. Focus is locked on the drill bit and pre-marked hole. Foreground shows scattered wood shavings creating depth, midground the drill chuck and hands, background softly blurred. Warm lighting remains stable. The carpenter positions the drill bit vertically over the mark, lightly touching the wood before drilling in. Fine wood dust spreads in a ring. Chinese The brief startup The camera remains mostly static with minimal pitch correction.
shot8: Shot 8 cuts hard to a medium close-up overhead shot. The workbench serves as a flat background, with several cut boards forming the initial shape of a box. A square placed at one corner creates a clear visual focus. Moderate depth of field ensures each board’s edge is visible. Warm lighting remains consistent. The carpenter performs a dry fit without glue, placing side panels together one by one, then pressing the square against the inner corner to check for perpendicularity. The box transitions from scattered pieces to a stable upright structure. The camera slowly lowers slightly to make the right-angle check more visible.
shot9: Shot 9 enters the key step via a brief hard cut, using a medium close-up eye-level shot. Foreground shows the glue bottle opening, midground the joint, background unused clamps. Under warm lighting, the glue reflects finely. The carpenter evenly squeezes wood glue along the joint, then closes the boards and quickly applies clamps. Chinese The squeezing The camera first gently pushes toward the joint, then slightly pans to the clamps, fully showcasing the joining process.
shot10: Shot 10 cuts hard with a slight time jump, using a close-up eye-level shot. Focus is on the box’s corner and sandpaper contact surface after clamps are removed. Foreground shows fingers and folded sandpaper edge, midground the box edge, background softly blurred. Warm side lighting makes dust particles faintly visible. After removing clamps, the carpenter carefully sands along the edge. The surface transitions from slightly sticky with glue residue and splinters to uniformly smooth.
shot11: Shot 11 transitions softly with a fade-in/fade-out from the previous shot, using a medium close-up side angle shot. Composition aligns brush movement direction with the wood grain of the box. Foreground shows bristles, midground the side of the box, background a softly blurred warm workshop. Lighting remains primarily natural side light plus warm lamps. The carpenter dips a small amount of wood wax oil and applies it evenly along the grain. The surface gradually shifts from matte to warm and subtly glossy. Chinese The fine brushing The camera slowly pans to highlight the coating application process.
shot12: Shot 12 fades in from the previous shot, using a medium-long static wide-angle pull-back at eye level. The composition centers the completed minimalist wooden box on the workbench as the visual focal point, with a few neatly arranged tools in the foreground creating a sense of instructional closure. The midground features the finished product, while the background reveals a tidy workshop. Warm, soft lighting unifies the scene with gentle tones. The carpenter gently lifts the box with both hands and slowly turns it toward the camera to display its four sides and interior space. The surface is smooth, edges are crisp, and the wood has a warm, lustrous finish. A Chinese summary appears simultaneously “关键步骤就是量准、划准、切稳、先试拼再上胶，最后细磨和上油”.
